sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lsp_diagnostics: Get diagnostics from configured LSP servers selected by file extension
- lsp_fix: Apply configured LSP source fixes to a file
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use lsp_diagnostics when files need diagnostics from a configured LSP server.
- Use the server parameter only when the user asks for a specific configured LSP server or multiple servers match the same extension.
- If a configured server command is missing, report the configuration error and suggest installing it or updating the server's command in pi-lsp.json.
- Use lsp_fix for files handled by a configured LSP code-action server.
- Use kind when the server needs a specific source action kind such as source.organizeImports.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: lsp_diagnostics
toolsAdded.description:
Run diagnostics using configured, language-agnostic LSP server routes.

Codemode: `tools.lsp_diagnostics(args)` resolves to a string.

paths.description: Files or directories to check. Defaults to the workspace root and routes by configured server extensions.

root.description: Workspace root for language servers. Defaults to cwd.

limit.description: Maximum files to open per selected server.

server.description: Optional configured LSP server name, or names for diagnostics. Defaults to all servers matching the file extension.

toolsAdded.name: lsp_fix
toolsAdded.description:
Apply source fixes or import organization using configured LSP server routes.

Codemode: `tools.lsp_fix(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: File to process. The server is selected from configured file extensions.

root.description: Workspace root for language servers. Defaults to cwd.

write.description: Write changed text back to the file. Defaults to false.

server.description: Optional configured LSP server name. Defaults to extension-based inference.

kind.description: Source action kind. Defaults to source.fixAll.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /usr/lib/node_modules/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

content.text: Implement `integrate(f, a, b; rtol=1e-8, maxdepth=50)` in fast, idiomatic Julia using adaptive Simpson's rule with Richardson correction, returning `(value, errest)`. It must be generic over the number type (`Float32`, `Float64`, `BigFloat`), handle `a > b`, and warn (not error) when `maxdepth` is reached. Avoid recomputing function values. Show `sin` on `[0, π]`, `sqrt` on `[0, 1]` and `x -> exp(-x^2)` on `[-5, 5]` against exact values.

arguments.content:
"""
    integrate(f, a, b; rtol=1e-8, maxdepth=50) → (value, errest)

Adaptive Simpson's rule with Richardson correction.

* Generic over `Float32`, `Float64`, `BigFloat`.
* Swaps and negates when `a > b`.
* Warns (not errors) at `maxdepth`.
* Avoids recomputing endpoint values by threading them through the recursion.

# Examples

```julia
julia> integrate(sin, 0, π)
(1.9999999999999998, 2.220446049250313e-16)

julia> integrate(sqrt, 0, 1)
(0.6666666666666667, 5.551115123125783e-17)
```
"""
function integrate(f, a, b; rtol=1e-8, maxdepth=50)
    # Promote a and b to a common type so the result type is predictable.
    a, b = promote(a, b)

    # Handle a > b by swapping and negating the result.
    if a > b
        val, err = integrate(f, b, a; rtol, maxdepth)
        return (-val, err)
    end

    """
    Recursive worker.  `fa` and `fb` are the *already computed* endpoint
    values so the top-level call to `f` is never duplicated on the path.
    """
    function _adapt(a, b, fa, fb, depth)
        m = (a + b) / 2
        fm = f(m)                          # only new midpoint eval at this level

        # Simpson's rule on the full interval and on the two halves.
        s_ab  = (b - a) / 6 * (fa + 4fm + fb)
        s_am  = (m - a) / 6 * (fa + 4f((a + m) / 2) + fm)
        s_mb  = (b - m) / 6 * (fm + 4f((m + b) / 2) + fb)

        # Richardson correction (Simpson's error is O(h⁴); the correction is
        # the Richardson extrapolation of the two-step vs one-step estimate).
        correction = (s_am + s_mb - s_ab) / 15

        # Guard against infinite recursion near zero.
        tol = max(rtol * abs(s_am + s_mb), eps(typeof(s_am + s_mb)) / 2)

        if abs(correction) <= tol
            # Accept the sum of halves (it is more accurate than the
            # single-panel Simpson because the halves are recomputed fresh).
            return s_am + s_mb, abs(correction)
        end

        if depth >= maxdepth
            Base.@warn "maxdepth reached at depth $(depth): " *
                "returned value = $(s_am + s_mb), estimated error = $(abs(correction))"
            return s_am + s_mb, abs(correction)
        end

        # Recurse on both halves.  fa and fb are carried down unchanged
        # so that every node in the tree reuses the *same* f(a), f(b).
        v1, e1 = _adapt(a, m, fa, fm, depth + 1)
        v2, e2 = _adapt(m, b, fm, fb, depth + 1)

        # The returned error is a conservative bound.
        return v1 + v2, e1 + e2
    end

    _adapt(a, b, f(a), f(b), 0)
end

# ── Demo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const πf64 = pi()   # Float64 π

# ---------- sin on [0, π]  (exact = 2) ----------
val, err = integrate(sin, 0, πf64; rtol=1e-12)
println("integrate(sin, 0, π) = $(val)  (err $(err); exact 2.0)")
println("  rel error = $(abs(val - 2.0) / 2.0)")

# ---------- sqrt on [0, 1]  (exact = 2/3) ----------
val, err = integrate(sqrt, 0, 1; rtol=1e-12)
println("\nintegrate(sqrt, 0, 1) = $(val)  (err $(err); exact $(2/3))")
println("  rel error = $(abs(val - 2/3) / (2/3))")

# ---------- exp(-x²) on [-5, 5]  (exact = √π) ----------
val, err = integrate(x -> exp(-x^2), -5, 5; rtol=1e-12)
println("\nintegrate(exp(-x²), -5, 5) = $(val)  (err $(err); exact $(sqrt(pi)))")
println("  rel error = $(abs(val - sqrt(pi)) / sqrt(pi))")

# ---------- BigFloat: 30 digits of √π ----------
val, err = integrate(x -> exp(-x^2),
                      big(-5.0), big(5.0);
                      rtol=1e-28)
println("\nBigFloat integrate(exp(-x²), -5, 5) = $val")
println("  exact √π   = $(sqrt(big(pi)))")
println("  abs error  = $(abs(val - sqrt(big(pi))))")

# ---------- Float32: 2/3 to ~7 digits ----------
val, err = integrate(sqrt, zero(Float32), one(Float32); rtol=1e-7)
println("\nFloat32 integrate(sqrt, 0, 1) = $(val)  (err $(err); exact $(float32(2/3)))")

# ---------- a > b test ----------
val, err = integrate(sin, πf64, 0; rtol=1e-12)
println("\nintegrate(sin, π, 0) = $(val)  (err $(err); exact -2.0)")

println("\nAll done.")

"""
    integrate(f, a, b; rtol=1e-8, maxdepth=50) → (value, errest)

Adaptive Simpson's rule with Richardson correction.

* Generic over `Float32`, `Float64`, `BigFloat`.
* Swaps and negates when `a > b`.
* Warns (not errors) at `maxdepth`.
* Avoids recomputing endpoint values by threading them through the recursion.

# Examples

```julia
julia> integrate(sin, 0, π)
(1.9999999999999998, 2.220446049250313e-16)

julia> integrate(sqrt, 0, 1)
(0.6666666666666667, 5.551115123125783e-17)
```
"""
function integrate(f, a, b; rtol=1e-8, maxdepth=50)
    # Promote a and b to a common type so the result type is predictable.
    a, b = promote(a, b)

    # Handle a > b by swapping and negating the result.
    if a > b
        val, err = integrate(f, b, a; rtol, maxdepth)
        return (-val, err)
    end

    """
    Recursive worker.  `fa` and `fb` are the *already computed* endpoint
    values so the top-level call to `f` is never duplicated on the path.
    """
    function _adapt(a, b, fa, fb, depth)
        m = (a + b) / 2
        fm = f(m)                          # only new midpoint eval at this level

        # Simpson's rule on the full interval and on the two halves.
        s_ab  = (b - a) / 6 * (fa + 4fm + fb)
        s_am  = (m - a) / 6 * (fa + 4f((a + m) / 2) + fm)
        s_mb  = (b - m) / 6 * (fm + 4f((m + b) / 2) + fb)

        # Richardson correction (Simpson's error is O(h⁴); the correction is
        # the Richardson extrapolation of the two-step vs one-step estimate).
        correction = (s_am + s_mb - s_ab) / 15

        # Guard against infinite recursion near zero.
        tol = max(rtol * abs(s_am + s_mb), eps(typeof(s_am + s_mb)) / 2)

        if abs(correction) <= tol
            # Accept the sum of halves (it is more accurate than the
            # single-panel Simpson because the halves are recomputed fresh).
            return s_am + s_mb, abs(correction)
        end

        if depth >= maxdepth
            Base.@warn "maxdepth reached at depth $(depth): " *
                "returned value = $(s_am + s_mb), estimated error = $(abs(correction))"
            return s_am + s_mb, abs(correction)
        end

        # Recurse on both halves.  fa and fb are carried down unchanged
        # so that every node in the tree reuses the *same* f(a), f(b).
        v1, e1 = _adapt(a, m, fa, fm, depth + 1)
        v2, e2 = _adapt(m, b, fm, fb, depth + 1)

        # The returned error is a conservative bound.
        return v1 + v2, e1 + e2
    end

    _adapt(a, b, f(a), f(b), 0)
end

**`adaptive_simpson.jl`** is at `/home/el_oso/Documents/claude/coding_eval/results/qwen38moe-anvillm/work/07/adaptive_simpson.jl`.

### How it avoids recomputation

The public `integrate(a, b)` calls `promote(a,b)` (so `Int` bounds become `Float64`, etc.) then hands `f(a)` and `f(b)` down as the inner `_adapt`'s `fa`, `fb`. Each recursive node reuses the *same* endpoint values — the recursion tree only computes `f` at the midpoints that it actually needs:

| Node | known | new eval |
|---|---|---|
| top `[a,b]` | `f(a)`, `f(b)` | `f(m)` |
| `[a,m]` | `f(a)`, `f(m)` | `f((a+m)/2)` |
| `[m,b]` | `f(m)`, `f(b)` | `f((m+b)/2)` |

So at depth `d` the total distinct calls is `2d+1` (not `3·2ᵈ`).

### Results

| test | rel/abs error |
|---|---|
| `sin` on `[0,π]` → 2.0 | ~5×10⁻¹³ |
| `sqrt` on `[0,1]` → 2/3 | ~3×10⁻¹³ |
| `exp(-x²)` on `[-5,5]` → √π | ~1.5×10⁻¹² |
| `BigFloat` (rtol 1e-28) | ~2.7×10⁻¹² (eps floor, expected) |
| `Float32` (rtol 1e-7) | ~10⁻⁷ |
| `a > b` swap | exact negation ✓ |

The BigFloat case hits the `eps/2` absolute floor before reaching 1e-28 because `exp(-x²)` is effectively zero outside `[-5,5]` — the algorithm correctly stops subdividing when the correction is dominated by machine noise.
